text: Hello everyone, welcome to our English class.I'm 蔡凤婷, nice to see you.Boys and girls, in this unit, you are going to learn something about the food we eat, and in this lesson, you are going to read a dialogue about dinner menu.Before we start our lesson, please make sure that you have these things, your student's book, your notebook, worksheet, and pens.Are you ready?Now, let's start.What is your favorite food?The following is my student John's favorite food.Look at the pictures.What are they?Please read after the recording.We usually use the plural form of noodle.We almost never eat a single noodle.Noodles are a kind of staple food.Please read after me.Can you name some other kinds of staple food?Yes, rice and bread.The second picture is prawn.AW or prawn.We can see seven prawns in the picture.Prawns are a kind of seafood.EAE, OO, Seafood.Can you name some other kinds of seafood?Yes, fish and crabs.The third one is bacon.BaconAA, BaconBacon is a kind of meat.Can you name some other kinds of meat?Yes, beef and chicken.The fourth one is cabbage.CabbageAA, A, I, CabbageCabbage is a kind of vegetable.Can you name some other kinds of vegetables?Yes, carrots and beans.Here, staple food, seafood, meat and vegetable are different food types.Now, Mrs.Lee, Ben and Kitty are talking with each other.Look at the title and picture and predict what they are probably talking about.They are probably talking about the food they would like for dinner.How do you know?From the title.Dinner menu.MenuMenu, 菜单Please take out your student's book and turn to page 55.Read the dialogue and try to answer the questions.What will Mrs.Lee do after she talks with Ben and Kitty?She will buy the food.What food material will she buy?Please circle the food material Mrs.Lee needs to buy.She needs to buy rice, prawns, garlic, tomatoes, eggs, bacon and strawberries.We know Mrs.Lee has some rice and eggs at home.So what else does she need to buy for her dinner?Please finish task 1 on your worksheet.Now, let's check.She needs to buy prawns, garlic, tomatoes, bacon and strawberries.We've known the food material Mrs.But what food would they like for dinner?Please read the dialogue again and finish task 2 on your worksheet.What food material will Mrs.Lee need to buy?Let's check.For staple food, they would like rice.For seafood, they would like steamed prawns with garlic.For eggs, they'd like fried eggs with bacon.For soup, they'd like tomato and egg soup.For fruit, they'd like strawberries.Well done!What would the kitty like for dinner?Let's read the dialogue for the third time and answer the questions.She'd like steamed prawns with garlic and fried eggs with bacon.GarlicGarlic means 大蒜SteamPlease read after me.E-A-ESteamAgain, steamHere, it's a verb which means 蒸FryPlease read after me.FryAgain, fryIt's also a verb which means 炸、煎、炒Steamed and fried are ways of cooking.Prawns and eggs are the main food.Garlic and bacon are other food.We usually add other food to the main food.And we use width to connect them.Now, let's say it together.Kitty would like fried eggs with bacon.Kitty would like steamed prawns with garlic and fried eggs with bacon.And would kitty like meat or seafood?Yes, she would like seafood.Yes, because she said, I'd like steamed prawns with garlic.We know prawns are a kind of seafood.And what does Mrs.Lee say to ask about Ben and Kitty's preferences?Would you like rice or noodles?Would you like meat or seafood?What kind of soup would you like?Tomato or cabbage?What kind of fruit would you like?Strawberries or apples?We have learned kind in unit 2.It is an adjective which means 友好的.But here it is a noun.It means 種類.We know tomato is a countable noun.Why isn't it tomatoes here?Here, tomato refers to tomato soup.And cabbage refers to cabbage soup.So we can also say, would you like tomato soup or cabbage soup?What about this sentence?We can say, would you like strawberries or apples?And we can also say the first sentence like this.What kind of staple food would you like?Rice or noodles?These are the two ways to ask about others' preferences.Lee is asking about Kitty's preference.Please finish the dialogue according to the pictures.What would you like for dinner?I'd like some seafood.What kind of seafood would you like?Prawns or fish?We can also say, would you like prawns or fish?I'd like steamed prawns with garlic.I'd like some eggs.Would you like steamed eggs or fried eggs?We can also say,What kind of eggs would you like?Steamed eggs or fried eggs?I'd like fried eggs with bacon.Good job!Please read the dialogue aloud after the recording.What would you like for dinner tonight?Here we use the rising tone and then the falling tone in the alternative questions.Let's read it again.I'd like rice for dinner.Here, I'd is the short form of I would.I'd also like some soup.Here, also is a net verb.It means year.Let's have tomato.It's my favourite.Alright, we'll have tomato and egg soup.I'd like fried eggs with bacon too.Mum, can we have some fruit after dinner, please?Yes, what kind of fruit would you like?I'd like strawberries.OK, but we need to buy some food first.Lee is good at cooking.These are what she cooked in the past.Lee cooked food in different ways.Steam, fry, boil.Boil, please read after me.Bake, please read after me.She cooked steamed eggs with meat.Fried chicken wings, please read after me.Again, wing.In Chinese, we say 翅膀.She also cooked boiled prawns.And baked potatoes with chillies.Now we've known four different ways of cooking and how to tell the names of the dishes.Peter and Simon are students at a boarding school.This is the dinner menu at the school canteen.They are talking about what they would like to eat.Please make up a dialogue.Remember to ask about the food type and the other's preference.Please check the description box for more information.Please subscribe to my channel.This is my student John's work.Let's read it.Simon, what would you like for dinner tonight?I'd like meat and vegetables.What kind of meat would you like?Would you like beef?Would you like beef or chicken?I'd like fried chicken wings.What kind of vegetables would you like?Fried cabbage or salad?I'd like fried cabbage.Okay, let's have fried chicken wings and fried cabbage.Did John ask about the food type?Did John ask about the other's preference?Yes, he has done a good job.I believe you've also done a great job.Boys and girls, let's sum up.In today's lesson, you've learned how to express the names of different foodsand how to pronounce the vowel pairs OO, EA and AW in different words.Also, you've learned how to ask about other's preferences and tell your own preference.Hopefully, you can ask about your family member's preferences and make your own dinner menu.After class, please complete the exercises on your homework sheet.So much for today.See you next time.Good night.
